title: The Crow and the Pitcher
originalTitle: The Crow and the Pitcher · English
sourceAuthor: Aesop; selected and told anew by Joseph Jacobs

artLabel: A thirsty crow drops small pebbles into a clay pitcher.
scenes: A Crow, half-dead with thirst, came upon a Pitcher which had once been full of water; but when the Crow put its beak into the mouth of the Pitcher he found that only very little water was left in it, and that he could not reach far enough down to get at it. He tried, and he tried, but at last had to give up in despair.
Then a thought came to him, and he took a pebble and dropped it into the Pitcher. Then he took another pebble and dropped it into the Pitcher.

Then he took another pebble and dropped that into the Pitcher. Then he took another pebble and dropped that into the Pitcher. Then he took another pebble and dropped that into the Pitcher. Then he took another pebble and dropped that into the Pitcher.
At last, at last, he saw the water mount up near him, and after casting in a few more pebbles he was able to quench his thirst and save his life.
Little by little does the trick.

pageArt.alt: The crow begins dropping pebbles one by one into the pitcher.
The risen water reaches the pitcher’s mouth and the crow drinks.
